title: Notre école dans la communauté
oneGoal: Students will identify their school as an important part of their local autumn community
decisionPoints: How familiar are students with the area around their school?
What community landmarks can students see from school windows?
Should we start with immediate school surroundings or broader community?
progression: Foundation lesson - establishes school as the center of community exploration in autumn
realWorldConnection: Our school is connected to many community helpers and neighbors who work together in autumn

title: Les personnes qui nous aident à l'école
oneGoal: Students will recognize the school community helpers who support their learning every day
decisionPoints: Which school helpers do students interact with most often?
Should we include volunteers or focus only on staff?
How do we show appreciation for school community helpers?
progression: Builds on Lesson 1 by identifying the helpers within the school community during autumn
realWorldConnection: Many people work together to make our school a safe, clean, and welcoming place to learn

title: Les changements d'automne dans notre communauté
oneGoal: Students will observe and describe how autumn brings changes to their local community
decisionPoints: What autumn changes are most visible in our local area?
Should we focus on natural changes or community activity changes?
How can students document autumn changes they observe?
progression: Builds on Lesson 2 by connecting seasonal changes to community life and activities
realWorldConnection: Autumn brings special changes that affect how our community looks, feels, and works together

title: Les gens qui nous gardent en sécurité
oneGoal: Students will identify community safety helpers and understand how they protect everyone in autumn
decisionPoints: Are students comfortable discussing safety without creating fear?
Which safety helpers are most visible in our community?
Should we include crossing guards and school safety helpers?
progression: Builds on Lesson 3 by introducing safety helpers who work to protect the community year-round
realWorldConnection: Safety helpers work every day, including during autumn, to keep our community safe and secure

title: Visite d'un pompier à l'école
oneGoal: Students will learn about fire safety and fire fighters' important community role through a special visit
decisionPoints: Can we arrange an actual firefighter visit or should we use virtual resources?
What fire safety concepts are appropriate for Grade 1?
How do we make the visit educational rather than just exciting?
progression: Builds on Lesson 4 by providing direct interaction with one type of safety helper
realWorldConnection: Fire fighters help our community stay safe from fires and other emergencies all year long

title: Les gens qui nous aident quand nous sommes malades
oneGoal: Students will understand how healthcare helpers support community wellness in all seasons
decisionPoints: Should we include mental health helpers or focus on physical health?
How do we discuss medical help without creating anxiety?
Which healthcare roles are most familiar to Grade 1 students?
progression: Builds on Lesson 5 by expanding to healthcare helpers who keep the community healthy
realWorldConnection: Healthcare helpers work to keep everyone in our community healthy and strong

title: Les gens qui apportent notre nourriture
oneGoal: Students will explore how food gets to their community and the helpers involved in this process
decisionPoints: Should we focus on local farmers or include broader food supply chain?
Which food helpers are most visible in our autumn community?
How do we connect autumn harvest to local food helpers?
progression: Builds on Lesson 6 by examining food system helpers who support community nutrition
realWorldConnection: Many helpers work together to bring fresh, healthy food to our community, especially during autumn harvest

title: Visite à l'épicerie du quartier
oneGoal: Students will observe food helpers in action and understand the grocery store as a community hub
decisionPoints: Can we arrange an actual grocery store field trip or virtual tour?
Which grocery store roles should we highlight for Grade 1?
How do we connect grocery shopping to community cooperation?
progression: Builds on Lesson 7 by providing direct observation of food system helpers at work
realWorldConnection: Grocery stores are important community places where food helpers serve families every day

title: Les gens qui gardent notre communauté propre
oneGoal: Students will appreciate sanitation workers and understand how keeping communities clean is everyone's job
decisionPoints: Should we include environmental helpers beyond garbage collection?
How do we emphasize student responsibility for community cleanliness?
Which cleaning helpers are most visible in our autumn community?
progression: Builds on Lesson 8 by introducing environmental helpers who maintain community cleanliness
realWorldConnection: Keeping our community clean requires helpers working together and everyone doing their part

title: Les activités d'automne dans notre communauté
oneGoal: Students will identify special autumn activities that bring their community together
decisionPoints: Which autumn activities are most common in our local community?
Should we focus on organized events or informal community gatherings?
How do we include diverse cultural approaches to autumn celebration?
progression: Builds on Lesson 9 by exploring how community members come together for autumn activities
realWorldConnection: Autumn brings special opportunities for community members to celebrate and have fun together

title: Promenade dans le quartier en automne
oneGoal: Students will observe their neighborhood community helpers and autumn changes through direct exploration
decisionPoints: Can we take an actual neighborhood walk or should we use virtual exploration?
Which community helpers are we likely to see during our walk?
How do we ensure student safety while encouraging community observation?
progression: Builds on Lesson 10 by providing direct community exploration and helper observation
realWorldConnection: Taking time to really look at our neighborhood helps us appreciate all the helpers around us

title: Les gens qui nous aident à nous déplacer
oneGoal: Students will explore transportation helpers who keep community members moving safely
decisionPoints: Should we include public transportation or focus on school transportation?
Which transportation helpers are most relevant to student experience?
How do we connect transportation to community connection and safety?
progression: Builds on Lesson 11 by examining transportation helpers who connect community members
realWorldConnection: Transportation helpers make it possible for people to move safely around our community

title: Les gens qui construisent et réparent
oneGoal: Students will understand how construction and repair workers maintain and improve their community
decisionPoints: Should we focus on new construction or maintenance and repair work?
Which construction helpers are most visible in our autumn community?
How do we connect building and repair work to community improvement?
progression: Builds on Lesson 12 by introducing workers who build and maintain community infrastructure
realWorldConnection: Construction and repair workers help make our community stronger and better for everyone

title: Comment nous pouvons aider notre communauté
oneGoal: Students will identify ways they can contribute to their community as young citizens
decisionPoints: What are realistic ways Grade 1 students can help their community?
Should we focus on individual actions or group community projects?
How do we build student confidence about their ability to make a difference?
progression: Builds on Lesson 13 by empowering students to see themselves as community contributors
realWorldConnection: Even young people can make important contributions to help their community be better

title: Créer une carte de notre communauté
oneGoal: Students will create a visual map showing important community helpers and places in their neighborhood
decisionPoints: Should maps focus on helper locations or general community landmarks?
What map-making tools are appropriate for Grade 1 students?
How do we help students represent their understanding of community geography?
progression: Extension activity synthesizing Lessons 1-14 by creating visual representation of community
realWorldConnection: Making maps helps us understand how our community is organized and where helpers work

title: Dessiner nos héros communautaires
oneGoal: Students will create artwork celebrating community helpers they've learned about
decisionPoints: Should students choose their favorite helper or draw multiple helpers?
What art materials will help students best express their appreciation?
How do we encourage detailed observation in student artwork?
progression: Extension activity building on all helper lessons by creating artistic celebration
realWorldConnection: Creating art about community helpers helps us remember and appreciate their important work

title: Jeu de rôles: Nous sommes des aides communautaires
oneGoal: Students will role-play being different community helpers to practice helper vocabulary and actions
decisionPoints: Which helper roles are most engaging and appropriate for Grade 1 role-play?
Should students choose their own roles or rotate through different helpers?
How do we keep role-play respectful and educational?
progression: Extension activity building on all lessons by practicing helper knowledge through creative play
realWorldConnection: Playing community helper roles helps us understand what different helpers do every day

title: Lettres de remerciement aux aides communautaires
oneGoal: Students will write simple thank you letters to community helpers expressing appreciation
decisionPoints: Which community helpers should receive student thank you letters?
What writing level is appropriate for Grade 1 thank you letters?
How do we ensure letters are delivered to real community helpers?
progression: Extension activity building on appreciation themes by creating authentic community connections
realWorldConnection: Thanking community helpers shows appreciation and builds positive community relationships

title: Célébration des aides communautaires
oneGoal: Students will plan and participate in a celebration honoring all types of community helpers
decisionPoints: Should we invite real community helpers to our celebration?
What type of celebration activities would best honor community helpers?
How do we ensure all types of helpers feel equally appreciated?
progression: Extension activity culminating unit learning by celebrating community helper diversity
realWorldConnection: Celebrating community helpers together shows our gratitude and builds community connections

title: Nous faisons partie de notre communauté automnale
oneGoal: Students will reflect on their learning and understand their important place in the autumn community
decisionPoints: How do we help students articulate what they've learned about community?
Should reflection focus on helper appreciation or student community belonging?
How do we end the unit with confidence about student community membership?
progression: Extension activity concluding the unit by celebrating student community belonging and civic pride
realWorldConnection: Understanding our community helps us feel proud to belong and excited to contribute as we grow
